title: I Posted the Neighborhood Compost Bin Photo After They Dumped Meat

parts.text: I opened the shared compost at 7:06 a.m. and a rotisserie chicken in plastic was staring back. The alley flyer, which the dumping neighbor had printed, said plant matter only. I was thirty-four, brownstone 2R, holding a caddy of peels. The chicken had a grocery sticker from the store two blocks west. I photographed sticker, flyer, and chicken. Then I posted in the building group with the caption per the flyer. At 7:12 the neighbor who printed it replied that one chicken is not a pattern.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The flyer author is defending a rotisserie as a one-off.

social.video_title: Plant-matter flyer, rotisserie in plastic — Part 1/2
social.description: Peel caddy, grocery sticker, alley smell. One chicken. Would you have named the store?

parts.text: The city compost inspector does patterns for a living. They left a warning on the bin, not on a doorbell, which still worked. The neighbor took the chicken to trash like an adult. The flyer stayed. I empty peels. Maggots did not get a vote. One-off is a word for when you get caught once. The sticker was a return address. I kept a copy. Plant matter is leaves, not lunch.

social.video_title: The inspector does patterns for a living — Part 2/2
social.description: Warning tag, chicken to trash, flyer still true. Was plastic a peel?
